item.title: FOMOS: Feature-Oriented Meshing of SDFs
item.description: arXiv:2611.17458v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce FOMOS, a purely geometric method for feature-oriented meshing of signed distance functions (SDFs) that addresses various challenges of the existing state-of-the-art methods. Our algorithm improves mesh quality and runtime, enabling the SDF meshing in a matter of seconds. While existing techniques such as Marching Cubes and Neural Dual Contouring either produce dense, low-quality triangulations or sacrifice details for sparsity, often requiring carefully chosen user parameters, our single-parameter FOMOS leverages feature sized sampling to dynamically adjust mesh resolution based on local feature size (LFS), which we compute efficiently by sampling a medial scaffold. The LFS considers not only curvature but also shape thickness and captures large features through non-local structure, omitting many redundant small triangles from existing methods. Through extensive comparisons, we demonstrate the distinct strengths of FOMOS in execution time, reconstructed result accuracy, and triangle quality in the output mesh. We also introduce a lightweight variant of FOMOS targeting huge ($10k^3$) sparse inputs, which, to the best of our knowledge, no existing method can handle except Marching Cubes. To demonstrate the usefulness of our method, we show that FOMOS enables instant previews using a sub-sampled medial scaffold and can accelerate volumetric simulations by orders of magnitude.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Ohrhallinger, Amal Dev Parakkat

item.title: Pose-based Neural Clothing for Animated Characters
item.description: arXiv:2611.18253v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Traditional garment simulation for animated characters is a time-consuming bottleneck for artists due to slow simulations and tedious parameter tunings.Recent data-driven methods offer a powerful alternative, capable of learning from a dataset of simulated data to generate high-quality deformations. A lightweight network design allows data-driven systems to achieve a real-time inference speed. This significantly improves the artist workflow, as they can interactively pose a character and see high-quality folds and wrinkles at animation time, thereby allowing to make creative decisions ahead of time. However, existing neural clothing methods have presented appealing results on datasets based on realistic human models (\eg SMPL), but when trained on animated character datasets, they struggle to generalize to unseen poses. In this paper, we aim at designing neural networks and training strategies to generalize better to unseen poses in real-time to enable the interactive posing applications. We focus on a production-oriented setting where the model is trained for a single garment in a quasi-static setup. Technically, we leverage a smooth, expressive latent space by first training a Variational Auto-Encoder (VAE). We then progressively train the VAE encoder to transition from reconstruction to pose-driven prediction. To guide this prediction, we condition the network on both low-dimensional pose parameters and character body surface displacements. Finally, we introduce a novel local gradient histogram loss that mitigates the over-smoothing effect of reconstruction losses. Extensive evaluations on production-level assets and public datasets demonstrate that our method produces sharp, realistic wrinkles, smooth large-scale drape, and temporal coherence in real-time, offering a robust and easily integrable solution for interactive posing workflows.
item.dc:creator: Julian N. Heidenreich, Vinicius C. Azevedo, Jakob Buhmann, Lento Manickathan, Arnold Moon, Paul Kanyuk, Amit H. Bermano, Jingwei Tang

item.title: TetraCoder: Adaptive Tetrahedral Encoding for Neural Fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.18267v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Implicit and explicit representations of geometry are central in computer graphics applications and come with their pros and cons. With surface sampling being faster on explicit representations and spatial queries being faster on implicit representations, finding efficient conversions between them is a highly desirable property. We present TetraCoder, a single resolution hash-free adaptive tetrahedral encoding that links an explicit tetrahedral spatial encoder with an underlying implicit signed distance field (SDF). The resulting hybrid implicit-explicit space is continuous piecewise affine (CPWA) by design, allowing to obtain an exact correspondence between the implicit SDF and the explicit analytic mesh. TetraCoder's design comes with additional perks, in particular: (a) it scales better than multi-resolution encoding methods due to its single resolution optimizable grid, (b) unlike hash-based methods, it is not affected by collisions, (c) it enables fast tetrahedral ray-tracing, geometry and appearance editing, directly through its adaptive tetrahedral scaffold. We demonstrate the versatility of TetraCoder by showing an improvement over state-of-the-art methods on multiple tasks: 2D/3D fitting from images and point clouds, 3D novel view synthesis, 3D reconstruction, and geometry/appearance editing.
item.dc:creator: Daniele Della Pietra, Antonella Rech, Nicola Conci, Nicola Garau

item.title: Creative Product Design under Brand Image Constraints
item.description: arXiv:2611.17762v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Industrial design requires creative visual exploration while satisfying constraints that are often product-specific and implicit. Existing text-to-image (T2I) approaches can generate creative designs through concept blending or multi-agent self-enhancement, but they provide limited mechanisms for ensuring that generated designs remain consistent with such constraints. We focus on brand image as a representative design constraint and propose a framework for brand-aware redesign generation. Given a product name, the framework constructs a brand image survey report that summarizes product and market information, derives a creative direction from the report, and integrates this direction into a self-enhancement loop in which generated images are critiqued and prompts are revised. We evaluate the framework on 50 redesign tasks across five product categories, comparing it with Naive T2I, IP-Adapter/IT-Blender, and unconstrained self-enhancement under the same T2I backbone. By a VLM-as-Judge protocol to measure creativity and brand identifiability, the proposed framework achieves a more favorable trade-off between the two objectives, with particularly clear gains in highly constrained categories such as automotive and motorcycle, where the plausible design space is relatively limited compared with that of other product categories. These results suggest that dynamically eliciting and textualizing brand image can guide creative product design generation under brand image constraints.
item.dc:creator: Takeshi Onishi, Hiroya Makino, Takahiro Yamaguchi, Hiroyuki Sakai

item.title: DIRT: Depth-completed Image-based Rendering using Two-band Blending for Live Novel-view Synthesis
item.description: arXiv:2611.18340v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: State-of-the-art novel-view synthesis (NVS) methods commonly require per-scene optimization before rendering, limiting their applicability in live settings. Live or ad-hoc NVS, however, demands low-latency rendering during capture and strong generalization to new scenes. Some previous work tried to address this task by adapting training- and optimization-based methods, trading quality for low latency. We introduce a live NVS approach following traditional image-based rendering that operates on a posed set of depth sensor observations and images. Our method leverages explicit, sparse point-based geometry obtained from active sensors, resulting in a sparsely filled depth buffer that is completed in the (novel) target view's screen-space. Using this proxy, a posed set of images is projected into the target frame before fusing the resulting observations through a frequency-aware two-band blending strategy. The pipeline is entirely non-neural and optimization-free, requiring no training data or scene-specific optimization. As a result, our approach reduces the delay between capture and novel-view rendering and does not rely on favorable network generalization. We validate the method's applicability to heterogeneous sensor setups - including handheld RGB-D cameras, automotive LiDAR, and thermal cameras - as well as challenging scenarios, such as low light captures. Our experiments demonstrate that the approach outperforms prior methods in live reconstruction scenarios, while maintaining competitive performance in conventional NVS benchmarks.
item.dc:creator: Mathias Harrer, Laura Fink, Noah Lewis, Paul Himmler, Tim Weyrich

item.title: Assessing the CAD Capabilities of General-Purpose AI Models: A Case Study of GPT-6 Astra
item.description: arXiv:2610.24451v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent advances in general-purpose AI models and agentic systems have enabled them to perform some CAD tasks. A systematic assessment is now needed to establish what these systems can accomplish and how well their outputs meet engineering requirements. This paper presents an empirical study of GPT-6 Astra, a SOTA general-purpose AI model, across four basic CAD tasks: model understanding, generation, editing, and evaluation. We design test cases spanning different levels of complexity and engineering requirements. The results show that GPT-6 Astra can support multiple stages of CAD workflows, with successful outcomes in cases involving nontrivial geometric complexity. This suggests that general-purpose AI is beginning to offer practical value in almost all steps in CAD workflow. However, gaps remain between generating visually plausible geometry and producing valid, functional, and editable CAD models. Recurring errors in freeform geometry, parameter dependencies, and mating relationships between parts limit engineering usefulness. Agentic iterative refinement can improve results but does not consistently resolve critical errors; long completion times further constrain practical use.
item.dc:creator: Qiang Zou, Jiajun Shen, Zhijie Yang, Yuhao Wang, Shitianyi Leng, Dongshuo Yin
